# WHY: consolidate_chemical_mappings.py seeds each run from its own prior
# output (load_existing_unified), which is additive — a corrected upstream
# grounding adds the right row but cannot remove the superseded one, so both
# persist. apply_retractions() drops the listed stale objects, but only when
# their sole contributing source is culturebotai_reviewed (attribution
# unambiguous); an object that has gained another source is left in place and
# 161 name->object rows spanning 16 unique stale objects. Verified: after
# dropping these objects, all 161 names still resolve to their now_asserted
# Only stale_object (the CURIE dropped) is required; other columns document
# provenance. Lines starting with # are ignored by the reader.
# 2026-08-14 (#784): the cobalamin row used to read
# i.e. it retracted CHEBI:30411 in favour of CHEBI:28911. That is backwards.
# CHEBI:30411 "cobalamin" is defined as the oxidation state being *unspecified*
# and is the direct parent of CHEBI:28911 "cob(III)alamin"; the source media
# list the bare vitamer name alongside Biotin and Thiamine. The +3 evidence was
# circular — AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY had copied the formula, InChI and
# SMILES out of CHEBI:28911 while the record was already mapped there, and a
# formula cannot select an oxidation state in any case (ChEBI records the same
# C62H88CoN13O14P for the +1, +2 and +3 forms, which differ only in the separate
# charge field). Upstream resolved this in CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#362
# and UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv now carries CHEBI:30411 in every column.
# The row is now name-level. CHEBI:28911 is a real ChEBI term with real xrefs
# (KEGG C05776, PDB-CCD B12); dropping the object would delete those. What needs
# retracting is the four bare-vitamer names that additive re-seeding left on it
# after the regrounding, which had left kgm.name:cobalamine with two exactMatch
